claim: Feeding Drosophila a high dietary sugar directs metabolic defects including obesity and organismal insulin resistance.

claim: The Hippo pathway regulates growth through the transcriptional co-activator Yki, a Drosophila homolog of mammalian YAP/TAZ.
source: The Hippo pathway regulates growth through the transcriptional co-activator Yki, a Drosophila homolog of mammalian YAP/TAZ (Huang et al., 2005).

source: The core pathway kinase effector Warts (Wts) phosphorylates Yki and inhibits its activity by sequestering Yki in the cytoplasm (Dong et al., 2007; Zhao et al., 2007; Oh and Irvine, 2008).

claim: Myc and cyclin E are well-established transcriptional targets of Yki in Drosophila.

claim: Myc and cyclin E were strongly elevated in eye clones of ras1G12V;csk−/− animals fed HDS.

claim: Myc and cyclin E were strongly elevated in eye clones of inrCA,ras1G12V;csk−/− animals fed a control diet.

claim: diap1 gene expression was strongly increased in the ras1G12V;csk−/− clones of animals raised in HDS compared to animals fed a control diet.
source: As previously reported, diap1 gene expression—assessed by the Yki transcriptional reporter diap1-lacZ—was strongly increased in the ras1G12V;csk−/− clones of animals raised in HDS compared to animals fed a control diet ((Hirabayashi et al., 2013) Figure 2A,B).

claim: diap1 gene expression was at most mildly increased in most ras1G12V;csk−/− clones in animals fed a control diet.
source: Upon closer examination, diap1 gene expression was at most mildly increased in most ras1G12V;csk−/− clones in animals fed a control diet (Figure 2A, arrowheads).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2A.

claim: The increase in Yki activity in ras1G12V;csk−/− clones of animals raised in a control diet was not sufficient to promote tumor overgrowth.
source: This increase in Yki activity was not sufficient to promote tumor overgrowth: ras1G12V;csk−/− clones of animals raised in a control diet were progressively eliminated from the tissue by apoptotic cell death (Hirabayashi et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work (Hirabayashi et al., 2013).

claim: ras1G12V;csk−/− clones of animals raised in a control diet were progressively eliminated from the tissue by apoptotic cell death.
source: This increase in Yki activity was not sufficient to promote tumor overgrowth: ras1G12V;csk−/− clones of animals raised in a control diet were progressively eliminated from the tissue by apoptotic cell death (Hirabayashi et al., 2013).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to previous work (Hirabayashi et al., 2013).

claim: Activation of insulin signaling pathway alone (inrCA) failed to elevate diap1 expression in a control diet.

claim: The triple combination (inr CA,ras1G12V;csk−/−) led to strongly elevated diap1 gene expression, including in animals fed a control diet.
source: However, the triple combination (inr CA,ras1G12V;csk−/−) led to strongly elevated diap1 gene expression, including in animals fed a control diet (Figure 2D).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2D.

claim: Activation of Yki is an emergent property of Ras and Src co-activation.
source: These results indicate that activation of Yki is an emergent property of Ras and Src co-activation, and increased insulin signaling further promotes Yki activity in Ras/Src-activated cells.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental results showing that Ras and Src together lead to Yki activation.

claim: Increased insulin signaling further promotes Yki activity in Ras/Src-activated cells.
source: These results indicate that activation of Yki is an emergent property of Ras and Src co-activation, and increased insulin signaling further promotes Yki activity in Ras/Src-activated cells.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental results showing that insulin signaling enhances Yki activity in Ras/Src-activated cells.

claim: The FERM domain protein Expanded (Ex) is both an upstream regulator of the Hippo pathway and a transcriptional target of Yki, forming a negative feedback loop.
source: The FERM domain protein Expanded (Ex) is both an upstream regulator of the Hippo pathway and a transcriptional target of Yki, forming a negative feedback loop (Hamaratoglu et al., 2006).
evidence: This claim is supported by citation to a previous study (Hamaratoglu et al., 2006).

claim: Removing a functional genomic copy of ex (ex+/−) did not affect normal eye tissue growth.
source: Removing a functional genomic copy of ex (ex+/−) did not affect normal eye tissue growth (Figure 2E).

claim: Reducing ex in ras1G12V;csk−/− animals (ex+/−,ras1G12V;csk−/−) dominantly promoted growth of Ras/Src-activated cells in a control diet.
source: Surprisingly, reducing ex in ras1G12V;csk−/− animals (ex+/−,ras1G12V;csk−/−) dominantly promoted growth of Ras/Src-activated cells in a control diet (Figure 2F-H).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2F-H.

claim: 40% of ex+/−,ras1G12V;csk−/− animals in control diet failed to initiate pupariation, dying as larvae with overgrown eye tissue.
source: As a consequence, 40% of ex+/−,ras1G12V;csk−/− animals in control diet failed to initiate pupariation, dying as larvae with overgrown eye tissue (Figure 2I).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2I.

claim: ex gene expression was strongly increased in ex+/−, ras1G12V;csk−/− clones of animals raised in a control diet, demonstrating Yki activation in these clones.
source: Immunostaining using anti-β-galactosidase antibody indicated that ex gene expression was strongly increased in ex+/−, ras1G12V;csk−/− clones of animals raised in a control diet, demonstrating Yki activation in these clones (Figure 2J).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 2J.

claim: Ras/Src-activated cells are functionally linked to Hippo pathway activity.
source: Together these results provide compelling evidence that Ras/Src-activated cells are functionally linked to Hippo pathway activity, as even a subtle perturbation of upstream Hippo signaling is sufficient to dominantly promote tumor Ras/Src-tumor overgrowth.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental results showing that perturbations in Hippo signaling affect Ras/Src-tumor growth.

claim: Even a subtle perturbation of upstream Hippo signaling is sufficient to dominantly promote Ras/Src-tumor overgrowth.
source: Together these results provide compelling evidence that Ras/Src-activated cells are functionally linked to Hippo pathway activity, as even a subtle perturbation of upstream Hippo signaling is sufficient to dominantly promote tumor Ras/Src-tumor overgrowth.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental results showing that reducing ex promotes tumor growth.

claim: Phosphorylation of Yki was significantly reduced in genotypically wts−/− eye tissues.
source: As anticipated, phosphorylation of Yki was significantly reduced in genotypically wts−/− eye tissues.

claim: Dietary sucrose did not alter Yki phosphorylation in lacZ-expressing control clones.
source: Dietary sucrose did not alter Yki phosphorylation in lacZ-expressing control clones (Figure 3A).

claim: In ras1G12V;csk−/− animals, HDS led to a reduction in Yki phosphorylation to a level comparable to loss of wts.
source: In ras1G12V;csk−/− animals, however, HDS led to a reduction in Yki phosphorylation to a level comparable to loss of wts (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Phosphorylation of Yki was reduced in eye tissues of inrCA,ras1G12V;csk−/− animals fed a control diet.
source: Phosphorylation was similarly reduced in eye tissues of inrCA,ras1G12V;csk−/− animals fed a control diet, indicating that increased insulin signaling is sufficient to suppress Wts kinase activity in Ras/Src-activated cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Increased insulin signaling is sufficient to suppress Wts kinase activity in Ras/Src-activated cells.
source: Phosphorylation was similarly reduced in eye tissues of inrCA,ras1G12V;csk−/− animals fed a control diet, indicating that increased insulin signaling is sufficient to suppress Wts kinase activity in Ras/Src-activated cells (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental data showing reduced Yki phosphorylation in inrCA,ras1G12V;csk−/− animals.

claim: No significant changes in total Yki levels were observed.
source: We did not observe significant changes in total Yki levels (Figure 3A).
evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3A.

claim: Ras/Src-tumors in the presence of HDS promote Yki activity through inhibition of Wts kinase activity.

evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental results showing reduced Yki phosphorylation.

claim: InR/Ras/Src-tumors in a control diet promote Yki activity through inhibition of Wts kinase activity.
source: Our results indicate that (i) Ras/Src-tumors in the presence of HDS or (ii) InR/Ras/Src-tumors in a control diet promote Yki activity through inhibition of Wts kinase activity.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental results showing reduced Yki phosphorylation.

claim: Reducing Akt activity through a hypomorphic allele of akt (ras1G12V;csk−/−,akthypo/hypo) reduced phosphorylation of Sav in animals raised on HDS.
source: Reducing Akt activity through a hypomorphic allele of akt (ras1G12V;csk−/−,akthypo/hypo) suppressed Ras/Src-tumor growth and reduced phosphorylation of Sav in animals raised on HDS (Figure 3—figure supplement 1).

claim: Tumor growth and phosphorylation of Sav was suppressed in inrCA,ras1G12V;csk−/−,akthypo/hypo animals fed a control diet.

evidence: This claim is supported by experimental data shown in Figure 3—figure supplement 1.

claim: In ras1G12V;csk−/− larval eye tissue fed HDS, activation of SIKs is mediated by Akt.
source: These results demonstrate that—in ras1G12V;csk−/− larval eye tissue fed HDS and inrCA,ras1G12V;csk−/− animals fed a control diet—activation of SIKs are mediated by Akt.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental results showing that reducing Akt suppresses SIK activity.

claim: In inrCA,ras1G12V;csk−/− animals fed a control diet, activation of SIKs is mediated by Akt.
source: These results demonstrate that—in ras1G12V;csk−/− larval eye tissue fed HDS and inrCA,ras1G12V;csk−/− animals fed a control diet—activation of SIKs are mediated by Akt.
evidence: This claim is inferred from the experimental results showing that reducing Akt suppresses SIK activity.

claim: Reducing SIK2/3 in ras1G12V;csk−/− animals (sik2RNAi,ras1G12V;csk−/−) suppressed diet-enhanced Ras/Src-tumor growth.
source: Reducing SIK2/3 in ras1G12V;csk−/− animals (sik2RNAi,ras1G12V;csk−/−) suppressed diet-enhanced Ras/Src-tumor growth (Figure 3B,C).
